messages:
maya: morning team :wave: quick question — who owns canary audience overrides for flags like `enable-new-routing`? We have org-level audience 5% but payments project wants 20%. Which takes precedence?
frank: short answer: narrower scope wins. Our effective precedence is (most specific -> least): model > route > project > org. So project override wins over org.
sasha: to expand — evaluation is two-step: 1) find most specific scope with an explicit `enabled` value and use that boolean; 2) if enabled is true at that scope, resolve `audience_pct` by searching most-specific -> least for an explicit percentage (inherit if missing). Example below.
maya: ok that helps. concrete example to confirm please.
frank: example 1:
```
flag: enable-new-routing
org: { enabled: true, audience_pct: 5 }
project: { enabled: true, audience_pct: 20 }
route: { }
```
Effective: enabled=true (project explicit), audience_pct=20 (project explicit).
sasha: example 2 (route disables):
```
org: { enabled: true, audience_pct: 5 }
project: { enabled: true, audience_pct: 20 }
route: { enabled: false }
```
Effective: enabled=false (route explicit) — audience_pct ignored because flag is disabled at the chosen scope.
ryan: guardrail note: platform enforces `org.max_canary_pct` to prevent projects from blasting to 100% unless ops gives an exception. So even if project asks 90% and org.max is 25%, the request should be capped. That lives in the policy service.
maya: good point — so precedence is about which config is authoritative but enforcement can clamp values.
sasha: edge case: model-specific flags. A model override (e.g., `model: redwood-1-beta`) should be the most specific and wins for both enabled and audience_pct if present. That lets product teams run model-targeted canaries without touching routes.
frank: another edge case: partial configs. If project sets `enabled` but not `audience_pct`, the platform should inherit `audience_pct` from org (or route/model if those are more specific and set it). Behavior: inherit the most specific available `audience_pct` below the chosen `enabled` scope? We should be explicit: after step 1 picks the boolean scope, step 2 searches from that scope downwards (more specific) then upwards for the nearest `audience_pct`. But simpler: search from most-specific to least for a percentage, independent of where `enabled` came from. That matches current implementation.
kim: thanks — I'll formalize the algorithm in docs and add unit tests for these patterns. Planning a small PR: updates `docs/feature-flags.md` and `flag-eval` tests. Assigning to myself.
frank: can you also add examples for mixing model & route scoped flags? I've seen confusion there.
kim: yes — will add 4 test cases: org/project/route/model mixes, boolean-only, pct-only inheritance, and enforcement of `org.max_canary_pct`.
deploy-bot: PR created: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/flags/pull/342 (branch: kim/flag-scope-docs)
frank: nice. @sasha and @ryan can you review when free? simple docs + tests. :thumbsup:
sasha: will take a look later today. quick question: who owns the canonical mapping of scope string -> priority list? platform or product? We should keep it in platform code with docs copied to product handbook.
ryan: platform owns the code + canonical doc. product teams can request exceptions via tickets.
maya: perfect. thanks all. That clears up the payments request — i'll reply to them with this logic and the guardrail note.
frank: one more operational note: when we change precedence rules we must run a migration to recompute active flags in the cache. Add a migration step in the PR checklist.
kim: noted, adding migration checklist + rollout playbook. I'll ping when PR is ready for review.
maya: thanks :pray:
